name: Saint Vincent & the Grenadines
summary: European treaty-making met an island that fiercely resisted it.
notes: British treaty title in 1763 did not mean complete control. Kalinago and Garifuna communities retained territory and fought colonial expansion. The main track represents Saint Vincent; the Grenadines were not politically uniform.

events.title: An English paper claim
events.detail: The Carlisle grant included Saint Vincent without English settlement.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: An Indigenous island recognized
events.detail: Anglo-French arrangements left Saint Vincent and Dominica to Indigenous peoples.

events.title: French settlement amid Indigenous autonomy
events.detail: French colonists lived alongside Kalinago and Garifuna communities; they did not uniformly govern the island.
events.uncertainty: Settlement was gradual and varied locally; not a clean transfer to France.

events.title: Britain receives treaty title
events.detail: France and Britain assigned Saint Vincent to Britain without Indigenous consent.

events.title: A treaty after the First Carib War
events.detail: Britain recognized a division of territory following Indigenous resistance.

events.title: French and Indigenous forces prevail
events.detail: A French expedition allied with local opponents of Britain took the colony.

events.title: British government restored
events.detail: The 1783 peace settlement returned the colony.

events.title: The Second Carib War ends
events.detail: British victory was followed by the mass deportation of Garifuna people in 1797.

events.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines independent
